78_marg1301: For it has happened to them, etc. It is set down in Proverbs with its exposition: “As a dog that returneth to his vomit, so is the fool that repeateth his folly.” And afterwards the apostle adds of his own: “And the sow that was washed, to her wallowing in the mire.” The dog, when he has vomited, casts out the food that weighed down his chest. But when he returns to his vomit, he is again burdened with that by which he had been relieved. So he who by confessing casts out the wickedness that pressed on the inmost part of his mind, after confession, when he repeats it, takes it up again. The sow, while she is washed in the mire, is made filthier. So he who laments his sin and yet does not forsake it subjects himself to a heavier punishment, since he has despised even the very pardon which he could have obtained by weeping, and has, as it were, wallowed himself in muddy water; because, while by his tears he withholds cleanness of life, he makes even those very tears foul before the eyes of God.

78_marg1304: Scoffers: mocking the faith and hope of Christians, because they vainly promise themselves a time of resurrection to come; walking not according to the catholic faith, but after their own lusts, rejoicing in new sins and saying: “Where is his promise?” They wish to bring this upon you, that you may believe all the promises concerning Christ to be vain. As if to say: What was foretold of him in the prophets has not been fulfilled in Christ. “Or his coming?” As if to say: What sign of his coming can you show? As if to say: No coming is to be. Therefore they do not believe in a coming to be, because “since the fathers slept,” that is, from the time of the resurrection, when the fathers, wearied with waiting for him, rested, when the resurrection of the dead first began to be preached. “All things”: the course and order of all creatures. So it continues, as now, and nothing has been changed, as a witness to his coming, and this from the beginning of creation. As it was in the beginning of the world, so it still is, and therefore they do not believe any coming to be.
78_marg1305: Paul, writing to the Thessalonians, restrains those who supposed that the day of the Lord was at hand. Peter rebukes those who assert that the coming and the promises of the Lord are delayed. Whence it is clear to all who love his coming that the mind must be held back in this opinion with greater moderation, so that we suppose neither that the day of the Lord is near and will come sooner, nor again that it comes more slowly. But let us take care of this alone, that whether he comes sooner or late, he may find us prepared when he comes.
78_interl3639: on the part of the foolish: there is no promise or coming, because since the ancient fathers died we see nothing changed in the world, nor will anything be changed except as it now is
78_interl3640: Here the apostle, on his own part
78_marg1306: They say that all things continue in the same manner, either because they truly do not know, or because they pretend not to know, that they may deceive you. There are two judgments of God: one by water, which is past; the other by fire, which remains. He says this is hidden from them: that the heavens, that is, this moist and turbulent air, of which it is said: “The kite in the air hath known her time,” were before, that is, among the first creatures of the world. Or “before,” that is, before the flood. And that the earth was before, consisting out of water, that is, by the removal of the water, which, by the word of God working, was gathered together into one place, and so the dry land appeared; and consisting through water, because by divine disposition it is all full of veins of water, as the bodies of living creatures are of blood, lest it fail through dryness if the watering by water should fail. “Through which two,” that is, in which two parts, the air and the earth, the world that then was, of another kind than this one, perished, overflowed with the water of the flood. For the flood did not reach the upper parts. But the heavens that now are, and the earth, by the same word of God, set in that form which they now have, are kept in store, reserved unto fire, to be changed for the better, against the day of judgment and perdition of the ungodly men.
78_interl3641: those who wish this: that there will be no judgment to come
78_interl3642: another translation: the heavens were of old, made from water and through water
78_interl3644: through which two, that is, in which parts: in air and in earth

78_marg1307: The earth perished, because, being submerged for so long a time, it ceased to bear fruit; afterwards also in very many places it received a face unlike that which it had had before. The heavens also perished, according to the appearance of this air. For the water filled all this space where the birds fly. There are also higher heavens, but whether these too are to perish by fire, or only those which perished even in the flood, is a question sometimes rather troublesome among the learned.
78_interl3646: after the flood, and are defiled by sins, are reserved so that they may be cleansed by fire with their evil inhabitants on the day of judgment
78_marg1308: Having proved that the judgment will truly be, he shows how effective it will be. If the false teachers tell you that you can do what you wish, because so much time remains until the day of judgment that the judge, through the length of time, will not be able to know many things, do not believe them, because whatever can be done in a thousand years he sees just as he sees what is done in one day. If they say that by doing penance for a thousand years you will not obtain pardon of your offences, do not believe it, because one day of true penance is worth as much as a thousand years, as with the thief. If they say it is not necessary to labour so long, you can rest for a day, do not believe it, because a thousand years of labour are not more sufficient for life than one day.
78_marg1309: And since the judgment is to be, therefore do not be led astray by the false teachers who say to you that even if there is to be a judgment, you still need not fear, because since there are so many thoughts and so many acts of men, if they must be examined one by one, thousands of years will not suffice, when the judgment is said to be in one single day, and so many things will be able to escape the judge. But let this not escape you: that one day is worth as much with God for doing something, as a thousand years are for men to do a single thing.
78_marg1310: In the knowledge of the divine power, things past, present, and future stand equally present; and the courses of time which seem long or short to us are of equal span with the maker of times, who beholds all things, great and small, equally. The Apostle therefore recalls this to convince those who said: “Where is his promise or his coming?” showing that God has by no means forgotten his promise or his coming. But since he so contemplates each day of our age with his eternal memory that he surveys the circuit of a thousand years, and a thousand years as the space of one day, without labour, it must be plainly understood that he knows most certainly the end of all those days and years, and without any doubt has also foreknown when the splendour of his coming is to be revealed, when the rewards promised to the saints are to be paid. Whence it is rightly added: “The Lord delayeth not,” etc.
78_marg1311: And because he sees all things, you can believe that the Lord does not delay in fulfilling his promises, because the time of fulfilling is not yet come, but at the time when he foresaw they should be fulfilled he will fulfil them. But he therefore defers, that he may first fill up the number of the elect which he foresaw. Whence in the Apocalypse: “And it was said to them, that they should rest for a little time, till their fellow servants” be filled up.

78_marg1313: That greatest fire will consume the four of which the world consists. Yet it will not consume all things so far that they cease to be, but two it will consume entirely, and the other two it will restore to a better form. Whence in what follows: “We look for new heavens and a new earth, according to his promises,” etc.

78_marg1315: He does not say other heavens, but the old and ancient ones to be changed for the better. Whence David: “They shall perish but thou remainest: and all of them shall grow old like a garment: and as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed.” What shall be changed? It is certain that, consumed by fire, when the fire soon departs they will take on a more pleasing appearance. Of fire and water we have nothing of the kind; rather we have in the Apocalypse: “And the sea is now no more.” We have also in the prophets: “The light of the lamp shall not shine to thee any more.”
78_marg1316: And the promises, etc. Allegorically. Do not believe those who say that nothing has been fulfilled of all that was promised about the birth of Christ, saying: Where are the new heavens and the new earth that were promised? We believe the new heavens to be those in which justice dwells, and the new earth those who bear the fruit of newness; and these we call the promises of God; or we, in whom justice dwells, and we know the truth: we look for the heavens, that is, the saints, to be new in the future, and a new earth, because he has promised.
78_marg1317: That is, at the time of the age to come. “Justice dwelleth,” because then to each of the faithful a crown of justice will be rendered according to the measure of the struggle, which cannot be done in this life.
78_marg1318: To him, that is, by the Lord: he alone is perfectly clean who is clean by divine judgment; for human judgments are often deceived.

78_marg1319: These are the watches of which it is said: “Blessed are those servants, whom the Lord when he cometh, shall find watching.” He watches who keeps himself free from filth, who, as much as is in him, has peace with all men, who subjects all the allurements of the flesh to the rule of the spirit, enjoying in himself a most happy peace.

78_interl3670: Do not think that the Lord delays the promise, but understand that the Lord therefore waits patiently so that more may be saved.
78_marg1320: He says that Paul wrote to them. In this he shows that what Paul wrote specially to certain churches, he wrote generally to all the churches that are throughout the world. Peter praises the wisdom of Paul. Paul says of himself: “I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church.” Paul humbles himself for his former unbelief and puts the innocence of the other apostles before his own. Behold, the first of the apostles, forgetful of his primacy and of the keys given to him, marvels at the wisdom given to Paul, because it is the way of the elect to marvel more at the virtues of others than at their own, and by these to stir themselves up to progress.
78_interl3673: of these things that I foretold you, that you may do these things that I taught
78_marg1321: He says that those things in the epistles of Paul are perverted by heretics, especially those in which he speaks of the grace of God which justifies the ungodly, that is, makes the just out of the ungodly. For he says: “Where sin abounded, grace did more abound.” Lest anyone should despair over sins committed, heretics so interpret it as to urge men to commit more sins, that through these they may receive greater goods. Against them Peter adds: You therefore, brethren, knowing before, because the unwise will bring in manifold errors: some denying the judgment to come, some falsifying the divine words, some interpreting badly, some loosening the reins of lust, and many other things.

78_marg1322: There is no book of the Old or New Testament in which heretics have not perverted something, whether by taking away, or by adding, or by changing. The only remedy for the unlearned is, with humble steadfastness, to give ear to the words of the teachers; and because heretics do not have this steadfastness, they are carried away from the Church by the wind of pride like light chaff; whence it is to their own destruction.
